e: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake hits East Nusa Tenggara, killing one person.
The People's Representative Council approves the appointment of Suyudi Ario Seto as Chief of the Indonesian National Police, succeeding Listyo Sigit Prabowo.
A flash flood hits Solok Regency in West Sumatra, killing two people and injuring four others. The disaster displaces around 480 residents and damages 98 homes and 12 government buildings.
President Prabowo appoints Suahasil Nazara as finance minister, succeeding Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa.
The passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 passengers, capsizes in the Java Sea while sailing from Surabaya to Banjarmasin, leaving six dead and 130 missing.
Eleven people are killed in a fire at a market in Paniai Regency, Central Papua.
A speedboat carrying five journalists covering the eruption of Anak Krakatau goes missing in the Sunda Strait along with its eight passengers.
Three people are killed in a collapse at an illegal gold mine in Sumbawa Regency, West Nusa Tenggara.
The Anak Krakatau volcano erupts, causing major flight disruptions in Jakarta.
A state of emergency is declared in Banyuwangi Regency due to a wildfire in the Ijen protected area.
Three volcanoes (Ibu, Lewotobi Laki-laki, and Semeru) erupt within a span of three hours.
A hiker dies after falling into the crater of Mount Slamet in Central Java.
Nine women are abducted by gunmen in Mimika Regency, Central Papua.
A magnitude 5.9 earthquake hits Central Sulawesi, killing one person.
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Flores, killing 136 people.
The ferry Putri Yasmin catches fire in the Lombok Strait, killing one person.

Authorities seize 1.3 tonnes of ketamine valued at 2.07 trillion rupiah (S$149 million) from the Tanzanian-flagged vessel MV King Sun, which originated from Thailand and was intercepted off the Riau Islands.
KMP Mutiara Sentosa 2, a ferry carrying 271 passengers and crew, catches fire off the Sapudi Islands en route from Surabaya to Makassar, leaving five dead and 41 missing.
State-owned oil company Pertamina adjusts the prices of several non-subsidised fuels, citing a decline in global crude oil prices and exchange rate fluctuations.
Perry Warjiyo resigns as Governor of Bank Indonesia, citing personal reasons. Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti is appointed as Acting Governor in accordance.
The United States imposes a 10% tariff on Indonesia, citing the presence of alleged forced labor in the supply chain.
An explosion occurs at a TNI ammunition depot in Madiun during routine maintenance and inspection, killing one soldier and injuring six others.

The passenger vessel KM Nurul Salsa sinks off the coast of Selayar Islands, South Sulawesi, after suffering engine failure. At least one person is confirmed dead, 49 are rescued, and 24 passengers and crew are reported missing.

A student at a school in Padang detonates a low-explosive homemade bomb in a classroom. No casualties are reported, but the student, who claimed to have been motivated by bullying, is taken into police custody.
A magnitude 5.1 earthquake hits Central Sulawesi, killing one person.
The West Papua National Liberation Army sets an airplane on fire and kills its American pilot after it lands in Yahukimo Regency, Highland Papua.

An explosion and fire occur at a herbal processing plant in the Candi Industrial Park in Semarang, killing one worker and injuring seven others. The blast is believed to have been caused by a malfunctioning sterilization tube due to excessive temperature and pressure.
An anti-corruption court in Jakarta convicts former education minister Nadiem Makarim of corruption over the Chromebook procurement scandal and sentences him to 10 years' imprisonment.
A magnitude 6.7 earthquake hits Central Sulawesi, killing three people.
Hundreds of students demonstrate against president Prabowo in response to a fuel price hike and mismanaged government spending on the Free Nutritious Meals program.

A court martial convicts four officers of the Indonesian Strategic Intelligence Agency for the acid attack on human rights activist Andrie Yunus in March and sentences them to three years' imprisonment.
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake with an epicenter off the coast of the neighboring Philippines hits North Sulawesi, injuring three people.
The rupiah reaches its lowest level against the US dollar with a ratio of to Rp 18,028 to $1.

President Prabowo dismisses Dadan Hindayana as head of the National Nutrition Agency amid criticism over food poisonings related to the Free Nutritious Meals program. Hindayana is arrested the next day along with two of his deputies.
Five people are killed in a suspected World War II ordnance explosion in a fishing village in Papua province.
A police raid on a commercial building in Jakarta results in the arrest of 321 foreign nationals on suspicion of involvement in illegal online gambling.
The Dukono volcano erupts in North Maluku, killing three climbers.
A bus collides with an oil tanker in North Musi Rawas Regency, South Sumatra, killing 16 people and injuring four others.
The Argo Bromo Anggrek train collides with a car transporting Hajj pilgrims in Grobogan, Central Java, killing four people.
Protests against East Kalimantan governor Rudy Mas'ud begin in Samarinda.
